helpful: The salience-band reached-rate table with its per-Term rows made the scored anchor unambiguous for a frozen high-band CVSG cell.
Provisioned petition/BIO/QP text was the decisive input — the BIO's top-hat vehicle argument is the main downward driver and only its text reveals it.
Web search cheaply resolved the companion-case signal (Rose v. PSA Airlines denied 2024 without CVSG), which the corpus and RECAP could not.
gaps: fedcourts query has no text/subject filter for SCOTUS rows, and the citation column is too sparse to retrieve a doctrinal line (the Mertens/Great-West/Amara/Montanile lookup returned zero rows); a QP-text or issue-area filter would have produced real comparables.

No statpack cut conditions the CVSG grant rate on the SG's eventual recommendation or on time-since-invitation; a CVSG-moment cell's whole uncertainty is the SG brief, and the pack is silent past the invitation itself.
SCOTUS docket entries for related petitions are absent from RECAP via the MCP endpoints, so companion-docket trajectories require the open web.
notes: The one corpus query cost 1,327 ranged GETs (~348 MB) to return zero rows; a cheaper miss on sparse filters would be kinder to the budget.
